subject: Chemistry
title: Addition of Halogens to Alkenes: the Bromine Test
summary: Ethene + Br₂ in CCl₄ gives BrCH₂–CH₂Br: the π bond breaks and one Br adds to each double-bond carbon, giving a vic-dibromide. The reddish-brown colour of bromine disappears, so the reaction is the lab test for unsaturation. Propene gives 1,2-dibromopropane and cyclohexene gives 1,2-dibromocyclohexane. Benzene fails the test: adding Br₂ would destroy its aromatic stability, so the colour stays.

notes.title: 09B – Addition of Halogens to Alkenes
notes.blurb: the reaction, the colour test for unsaturation, examples, the benzene trap and solved examples

keyPoints: CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ (CCl₄) → **BrCH₂–CH₂Br**: the π bond breaks; one Br on **each** double-bond carbon.
The product is a **vic-dibromide** (Br on adjacent carbons). CCl₄ is an **inert solvent**.
Br₂ is **reddish-brown**; the dibromide is **colourless**: the colour is discharged → **test for unsaturation**.
**Benzene fails:** resonance makes it aromatic; adding Br₂ would break aromaticity, so the colour stays.

blocks.p: The **π bond** of the double bond breaks and one bromine atom adds to **each of the two adjacent carbons**. The product, with the two halogens on neighbouring carbons, is a **vicinal (vic-) dibromide**. CCl₄ is only an **inert solvent**.

sections.h: The colour test: test for unsaturation

blocks.p: As bromine adds to the alkene, its reddish-brown colour is **discharged**. This decolourisation shows that a **C=C double bond** is present: the **test for unsaturation**.
**Break the π bond and put one Br on each of the two carbons of the double bond.** Other carbons are not touched.

Benzene is drawn with three C=C bonds but does **not** decolourise Br₂/CCl₄. Its π electrons are delocalised by **resonance**, which makes it **aromatic** and especially stable. Adding Br₂ would destroy the aromaticity, so no addition occurs and the **reddish-brown colour stays**.

simulation.reason: A fixed reaction and colour test shown in the video; no continuous variable for the student to explore.
